subject: microbiology
title: HHV-8, Kaposi Sarcoma and Herpesvirus Latency

steps.tx: **HHV 8**, also called Kaposi sarcoma associated herpesvirus, is a gamma herpesvirus transmitted mainly by saliva and, less efficiently, sexually or by blood and organs. Infection is often silent when cellular immunity is intact. The virus persists in B cells and infects endothelial lineage cells in lesions, blending viral oncogenes with inflammatory cytokines to create the spindle cell proliferation of Kaposi sarcoma.
steps.say: HHV 8 is necessary for Kaposi sarcoma, but immune failure lets the disease appear.

left.title: Virus biology
points: Saliva is the main transmission route
Lytic reactivation contributes inflammatory viral proteins

right.title: Permissive settings
points: Advanced HIV with low CD4 count
Classic disease in older Mediterranean and Eastern European men
Endemic disease in parts of sub Saharan Africa

steps.tx: **Kaposi sarcoma** forms violaceous macules, plaques, nodules and oedematous lesions driven by spindle cells, slit-like vessels, extravasated red cells and inflammation. Lesions may involve mouth, gut and lungs. Skin appearance can suggest the diagnosis but biopsy confirms it when presentation is atypical. Visceral symptoms, ulceration and lymphoedema determine staging and treatment urgency more than lesion count alone.
steps.say: Purple vascular skin lesions plus immunosuppression should trigger Kaposi assessment and biopsy when uncertain.

right.title: Assessment
points: Ask about cough, dyspnoea and gastrointestinal bleeding
Stage HIV, CD4 and organ involvement

steps.tx: The shared herpesvirus property in the plan is **latency**: viral genome persists in host cells with restricted gene expression and periodic reactivation. HSV hides in neurons, VZV in ganglia, EBV and HHV 8 in B cells, and CMV in myeloid progenitors. Latency is not eradication, and loss of T-cell surveillance can change a silent viral reservoir into proliferative or lytic disease.
steps.say: Each herpesvirus chooses a latency address, and immune control keeps that address quiet.

left.title: Latency reservoirs
points: HSV and VZV in sensory ganglia
HHV 8 in B cells and lesion spindle cells

right.title: Reactivation triggers
points: Local stress or ultraviolet exposure for HSV

steps.tx: HHV 8 also causes **primary effusion lymphoma**, multicentric Castleman disease and KSHV inflammatory cytokine syndrome. These are distinct presentations of viral driven B cell and cytokine pathology. Fever, effusions, lymphadenopathy, splenomegaly, cytopenias and high inflammatory markers can overlap. Diagnosis combines imaging, fluid or node pathology, HHV 8 staining and viral load in specialist pathways, not serology alone.
steps.say: HHV 8 can drive tumours and cytokine storms, not Kaposi sarcoma alone.

left.title: B cell disorders
points: Primary effusion lymphoma in body cavities
HHV 8 positive diffuse large B cell lymphoma
LANA nuclear staining confirms infected tumour cells

right.title: Inflammatory presentations
points: KICS with high viral load and cytokines
Must separate infection and lymphoma progression

steps.tx: Effective **antiretroviral therapy** is central in HIV associated Kaposi sarcoma and can cause lesion regression as CD4 control recovers. Reducing immunosuppression may help transplant disease, balanced against graft rejection. Local therapy suits limited lesions, while systemic chemotherapy is used for symptomatic visceral, rapidly progressive or refractory disease. Immune reconstitution inflammatory worsening may occur after ART initiation and needs expert distinction from progression.
steps.say: Restoring immune control is treatment, not merely background, in HHV 8 disease.

nodes.label: Confirm lesion and stage organ disease
Start ART or reduce excess suppression
Local or systemic therapy by burden

steps.tx: Antiviral drugs have limited direct impact on latent HHV 8 because latency expresses few lytic targets and established Kaposi sarcoma is a vascular tumour sustained by viral and host growth signals. Ganciclovir can reduce lytic replication in selected settings but is not standard KS therapy. The key lesson is to treat **host immunity, tumour burden and complications** rather than expecting herpes antivirals to erase latent virus.
steps.say: Latent HHV 8 is not cured by standard herpes antivirals; immune and tumour therapy lead.

left.title: What helps
points: Local radiation, intralesional or surgical care in selected lesions

right.title: What does not
points: Expecting serology to monitor lesion activity alone
Stopping ART because lesions flare during early immune recovery
